Title: Govt studying specific law to tackle ticket scalping
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, together with the Communications Ministry and relevant agencies, is reviewing specific legislation to address ticket scalping activities.
Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the effort is important to curb individuals who bulk-purchase tickets, including through the use of automated bots, before reselling them at significantly higher prices.
She said such activities not only force consumers to pay exorbitant prices but may also expose them to the risk of fraud when purchasing tickets from unofficial sellers.
"Many people are now excited to get tickets for the 2026 Sepang Formula 1, which will take place next month. So, please be careful when making purchases," she posted on Facebook today.
Purchasing tickets from unofficial sellers could result in consumers receiving counterfeit tickets, tickets that have already been used, or tickets that have been cancelled by the organiser, she added.
In this regard, consumers are advised to check official sales channels, the original ticket prices, the seller's identity, as well as the terms and conditions governing ticket use before making payment.
"Do not easily believe screenshots or pressure tactics such as 'pay now before someone else takes it'," she said.
Meanwhile, consumer awareness remains the first line of defence in addressing ticket scalping, as long as there are people willing to buy from scalpers, the activity will continue.
"Use your power as a consumer. Do not buy from ticket scalpers, do not give in to exorbitant prices and do not let your excitement cause you to become a victim," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Aireen Omar named AI Malaysia chairperson
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Aireen Omar, former AirAsia Bhd chief executive officer, has been appointed chairperson of AI Malaysia Bhd, the government's newly established agency tasked with spearheading and coordinating Malaysia's national artificial intelligence (AI) agenda.
Her appointment comes as AI Malaysia moves to strengthen its institutional structure following its launch by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on July 28.
In a statement, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said Aireen, who currently serves as a board member of Tune Protect Group Bhd and an adjunct professor at Universiti Malaysia Sabah, brings more than 20 years of experience in business transformation, technology and regional growth to the newly-established agency.
Her current work focuses on supporting high-growth technology ventures and founders, with expertise spanning venture scaling, AI and digital transformation, capital strategy, corporate governance and market expansion across Asean.
As the ministry's lead agency for AI, AI Malaysia is tasked with coordinating the national AI agenda, promoting safe and responsible AI adoption and driving the National AI Action Plan 2026–2030 towards achieving AI Nation 2030.
Gobind said the appointment of AI Malaysia's inaugural board marked an important milestone in strengthening the institutional foundation for Malaysia's national AI agenda.
He said the inaugural board brings together leaders from the public and private sectors, with experience spanning national transformation and public policy, digital economy development, investment and AI innovation, bringing complementary perspectives from government and industry.
"The establishment of AI Malaysia provides the nation with a dedicated institution to lead and coordinate its AI agenda.
"The appointment of the board brings strategic leadership, sound governance and diverse public- and private-sector perspectives to this mandate," he said.
Gobind added that the appointment further strengthens AI Malaysia's institutional capacity and governance as it advances its national mandate, moving the country's AI agenda from strategy to coordinated implementation and impact, anchored in accountability and the nation's long-term interests.
The other directors are Digital Ministry secretary-general Datuk Fabian Bigar, deputy secretary-general (Digital Development) Ma Sivanesan Marimuthu, Employees Provident Fund chief digital technology officer Muhammad Afhzal Abdul Rahman and Trendcell Sdn Bhd chairperson and MyTeksi Sdn Bhd director Foo Yen Ling Adelene.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Porsche driver escapes unhurt after sports car consumed by flames at Lanchang toll plaza
Article:
TEMERLOH: A Porsche sports car, believed to be a Cayman, was completely destroyed by fire at the Lanchang toll plaza exit ramp here today.
The driver, however, escaped unhurt.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations, Mohd Salahuddin Isa, said firemen were alerted to the incident at 1.04pm.
He said that a team of eight firefighters from the Mentakab Fire and Rescue Station, along with a Fire Rescue Tender vehicle and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services unit, was
dispatched to the scene.
"The team arrived at the location at 1.42pm after travelling approximately 35 kilometres.
"Upon arrival, it was found that the fire involved a Porsche car, which was 100 per cent burnt," he said in a statement today.
He said the operation to extinguish the flames was carried out using a hose reel line drawing water from the fire engine's tank.
The fire was brought under control by 2.08 PM before being completely extinguished.
"No casualties were involved in the fire, and the vehicle driver was confirmed safe," he said.
At press time, no information was available on how the incident occurred.

Title: New York marks 25th anniversary of 9/11 attacks
Article:
NEW YORK: New York commemorates the 25th anniversary of the devastating Sept 11, 2001 attacks Friday with a ceremony marked by US President Donald Trump's absence and right-wing outrage at the attendance of the city's first Muslim mayor.
[[nid:1530584]]
Trump will pay his respects at the Pentagon, not New York, where hijacked planes destroyed the World Trade Centre and killed most of the 2,977 total victims on that world-altering day.
Vice President JD Vance and Trump's four living predecessors – Republican George W. Bush, who was in office during the attacks, and Democrats Joe Biden, Barack Obama and Bill Clinton – are all expected at the "Ground Zero" site in lower Manhattan.
No one will give speeches at the ceremony, while bereaved family members will read out the names of all of those killed and a bell rung to mark major moments during the attack.
"Memorials like this and discussions about those events are an important part of keeping it alive and understanding how we prevent tragedies like this from ever happening again," said Robert Kafka, a Chicagoan in his 60s visiting the 9/11 Memorial.
Alongside the former presidents will be Democratic Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the Big Apple's first Muslim mayor, despite a campaign urging him to stay away spearheaded by the right-wing New York Post and former mayor Rudy Giuliani.
A petition, which has gathered more than 100,000 signatures, accuses Mamdani of associating with unspecified individuals who are "dismissive of American institutions or insufficiently critical of extremist ideologies."
"It's concerning to me that the mayor is being treated differently simply because he is Muslim," city council member Shahana Hanif told CNN.
[[nid:1530583]]
Mamdani won plaudits however for recently revealing thousands of documents showing what city officials knew about toxicity levels of the air in Lower Manhattan following the attacks.
After the initial dust cloud that followed the collapse of the World Trade Center, months of pollution and lingering dust ensued, causing cancers from which thousands of New Yorkers still suffer today.
[[nid:1530582]]
- 'TOXIC AIR' -
"People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied and told them they were safe to breathe in toxic air," Mamdani said Tuesday.
Nineteen Al-Qaeda operatives hijacked four planes on that nearly cloudless day in 2001. Two jets slammed into the World Trade Centre's Twin Towers, causing the iconic 110-story buildings to collapse.
A third plane struck the Pentagon, while a fourth crashed into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers fought back.
Beyond those killed on Sept 11, more than 9,400 other people have died from 9/11-related illnesses, according to the federal program established to provide medical care to those affected.
Some 100 million Americans were not even born or are too young to remember the tragic events.
Logan Miller, 32, lost his uncle during the attacks, and his grandfather to 9/11-related illness in the aftermath.
"I think the next generation just can't fathom what actually transpired and how someone could be impacted by that, and so I actually find them asking more questions," he told AFP.
Huge crowds are expected to gather in Lower Manhattan for the memorial service.
The Secret Service has erected a security ring of steel around the site of the 9/11 Memorial and Museum.
Police commissioner Jessica Tisch said an anti-drone team would be deployed as a precaution, but stressed there was no intelligence of a specific threat to the gathering.
Al-Qaeda meanwhile has marked the anniversary by releasing a video showing images of late leader Osama bin Laden and his son Hamza, who Trump said in 2019 had also been killed.
Ahead of the memorial, a drone show with 2,977 lights rose above New York Harbor, one for each person killed in the attacks.--AFP PIC
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MMEA conducts 720,000 inspections, detains 4,401 since 2023
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) has carried out about 720,000 inspections and 161 searches since 2023, detaining 4,401 people as part of efforts to combat cross-border crimes in the country's waters.
MMEA Maritime Security and Surveillance Division Border Security and Data Branch principal assistant director Commander Mohd Khairul Azhar Isahak said illegal fishing, smuggling and the entry of illegal immigrants were among the main threats being tackled by the agency.
"Over the MMEA's 21-year history, illegal fishing has remained one of the main threats, involving both unlicensed local fishermen who are unfamiliar with the regulations and foreign fishermen.
"Of the 4,401 people detained since 2023, more than 3,100 were involved in illegal fishing, smuggling and the entry of illegal immigrants," he said while appearing as a guest on Bernama TV's Apa Khabar Malaysia programme.
Khairul said the effectiveness of MMEA operations depended greatly on cooperation from the maritime community, particularly fishermen, who played a key role as the agency's 'eyes and ears' in detecting suspicious movements and activities at sea.
He urged the maritime community to channel information on suspicious activities to the MMEA, including details of locations, times of incidents and suspicious boats or vessels, instead of taking matters into their own hands, which could pose safety risks.
"The Sahabat Maritim programme has been implemented nationwide to strengthen ties between the MMEA and the maritime community. As they are at sea almost every day, they are often more familiar with the waters than MMEA personnel themselves," he said.
On asset enhancement, Khairul said the MMEA would continue to strengthen its operational capabilities through the acquisition of two Multi-Purpose Mission Ships (MPMS) from Turkiye, which would allow the agency to conduct operations further out in national waters for extended periods.
He said the MMEA had received an AW189 helicopter for nationwide deployment and was finalising the procurement of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) to enhance monitoring and surveillance capabilities in national waters.
Khairul said the MMEA, through the Home Ministry, was also planning to acquire coastal radar systems for several strategic areas, particularly in Sarawak and along the east coast of the peninsula, to address gaps in surveillance coverage.
He said the coastal radars were capable of detecting vessel movements up to 50 to 60 nautical miles away, enabling the MMEA to identify suspicious activities at an early stage and deploy the nearest assets more quickly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Umno must end internal bickering, strengthen unity, says party delegate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno should strengthen unity within the party and put an end to internal bickering and "backstabbing" as it rebuilds its political strength.
Johor Umno delegate Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said grievances should be raised through proper party channels instead of being discussed behind the backs of leaders and members.
Fared, who is Parit Sulong Umno deputy chief, said members who were unhappy with any decision should voice their concerns in meetings or through delegates rather than create divisions within the party.
"If there are grievances, state them in our meetings. Put them in writing. Raise them through the delegates in our respective divisions.
"Do not talk behind people's backs, and worse still, do not stab each other in the back," he said while debating the Umno president's policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
The Semerah assemblyman said Umno's recovery would depend on its leaders and members working towards a common direction rather than operating independently.
He said all levels of the party had a role and responsibility in strengthening Umno and ensuring its machinery remained united.
"Every leadership has a role and responsibility. Each of us must move according to the same guidance.
"We must unite our thinking, leadership and our approach. Umno cannot stand separately. It must be one, and its membership must also be united," he said.
He also urged party members to respect decisions reached through formal meetings and avoid disputing them afterwards.
Fared also highlighted the Rumah Bangsa initiative, saying former members who had left or distanced themselves from Umno remained keen to return and contribute to the party.
He said the initiative should continue providing space for them to return and serve alongside existing members.
"The people outside this hall miss Rumah Bangsa. Bring them back to serve together. What matters is that they are with us," he said.
He said rebuilding Umno's strength required the party to welcome back those who remained committed to its struggle, regardless of whether they had previously held positions.
Fared also reminded members that political and personal differences should not be allowed to weaken the party's unity.
He said Islam and democracy required members to respect one another and work together despite their differences.
He also referred to the danger of division, stressing that internal disputes could weaken Umno's ability to face future political challenges.
He said the party's various efforts, including Rumah Bangsa and its broader political initiatives, would only succeed if members shared the same objective of strengthening Umno and the country.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Numbak fire victims receive RM1,500 special federal aid
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today presented RM1,500 in special federal aid to each of the 111 heads of households affected by the Numbak fire.
The aid was distributed during his visit to the temporary relief centre at Damai Multipurpose Hall, where he met victims and assessed their conditions.
Each household head received RM1,000 from the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and RM500 from the Prime Minister's Department Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU).
Anwar also handed over Nadma food baskets to the victims, who lost their homes in the blaze.
The visit provided Anwar an opportunity to hear directly from the victims about their needs while staying at the relief centre.
The fire at 1.40am on Aug 30 destroyed 202 homes and claimed the lives of three children — Mohd Asrul Abdullah, 6, Nana Abdullah, 4, and Nur Farah Bilah Mohd Tajah, 8.
The
blaze
razed a stilt settlement covering Kampung Lok Buta, Kampung Lok Poring and Kampung Sabang Lama, spanning an estimated 260 metres by 380 metres.
Anwar visited the centre before departing for Kota Kinabalu International Airport.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas welcomes 'blue-green' cooperation
Article:
KOTA BARU: Pas welcomes efforts to strengthen cooperation with Barisan Nasional or the 'blue-green' cooperation, but several matters still need to be refined before any decision can be made.
Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the party believed any differences could be resolved if all parties were sincere and adhered to principles outlined by Allah.
"There are still many matters that need to be refined, and I believe whatever problems arise can be resolved if all parties are sincere and return to the principles outlined by Allah," he said.
The Perikatan Nasional deputy chairman said Pas would discuss the matter at its party meeting before it was brought to the party's Syura Council for consideration.
"Pas holds its party meetings every month, but matters concerning cooperation will be decided according to necessity.
"Perhaps the upcoming Melaka election could be the first focus," said the Kubang Kerian member of parliament.
Tuan Ibrahim said Pas had long championed the agenda of penyatuan ummah (Muslim unity) for the future of Muslims and Malays in Malaysia.
He said the concept was not new and remained an important agenda for the party.
"Pas has championed the agenda of penyatuan ummah for the future of Muslims and Malays in Malaysia.
"This is not a new idea," he said.
Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hinted today that Barisan Nasional could undergo an "evolution" if it forges a
strategic partnership
with another political force.
Without naming any party or political coalition, the BN chairman said such a development could occur, particularly when 'blue' meets 'green'.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka assembly dissolution 'not far off', says Rauf
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Melaka state assembly could be dissolved soon, with Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh saying the time was "not far off".
Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the 2026 Umno general assembly here today, Rauf said preparations for the state election had been under way for the past two years.
Asked if the state assembly would be dissolved this month, he said: "InsyaAllah (God willing)."
"Not long from now. When the time comes, I will announce it, but the timing is neither too long nor too short.
"Our preparations have been under way for the past two years. We are just waiting for the right moment, the final stages of wrapping up these preparations, before we begin the process of dissolving the assembly," he said.
On political cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and other parties, Rauf, who is also the state BN chairman, said Melaka's political landscape was different from that of other states as the state government was based on the BN Plus formula.
"We will leave it to the people to decide who the best strategic partner for the Melaka state government is," he said.
He also reiterated that BN would contest all 21 seats it currently holds in the state assembly.
He said no negotiations had been held with other parties, as any discussions would only take place after the dissolution of the state assembly.
"We have not begun negotiations because I have stressed that any negotiations with any political party will only be held after the dissolution of the state assembly.
"We cannot compromise on these 21 seats by sharing them with others. We will contest in our respective seats.
"As for the other seven seats, the parties that won them should contest and defend their seats. We will defend the seats that we won," he said.
On Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's policy speech at the assembly, Rauf described it as a good speech that charted a new direction for the party to regain its dominance ahead of the 16th general election.
"The president's speech today was good. It showed a new direction for Umno to remain dominant ahead of the 16th general election.
"Certainly, this new spirit must be embraced by all Umno leaders at the grassroots level so that we can no longer be a party that merely fills the numbers, neither here nor there.
"Umno must regain its dominance to lead the government," he said.
When asked about possible collaboration between the 'blue' and 'green' parties, Rauf said any formal decision regarding inter-party alliances remained subject to the top leadership's direction and official decisions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asean, South Korea join forces on AI, digital health for resilient regional care
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Asean member states and South Korea are moving to deepen cooperation in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital health, with the shared goal of building a more connected, secure and resilient regional healthcare ecosystem to improve access to care and strengthen early disease detection.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad described South Korea as an invaluable partner in advancing Asean's digital health agenda, calling the collaboration a crucial step towards a shared vision of an Asean that works together for equitable, future-ready health systems.
"The pandemic underscored the vital need for resilient and adaptive healthcare. Today, we stand at the intersection of public health and rapid technological innovation.
"By leveraging AI, data-driven insights and digital solutions, we can bridge equity gaps, strengthen early warning systems and ensure high-quality healthcare reaches every community, even at the corners of our region," he said in his opening remarks while chairing the 3rd Asean–Republic of Korea (ROK) Health Ministers' Meeting, convened during the 17th Asean Health Ministers' Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings.
Dzulkefly said initiatives such as Korea's Big Data Policy, the technical expertise of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) and Korea Human Resource Development Institute for Health and Welfare (KOHI), offered proven approaches in medical AI and digital primary care.
"By aligning our policy goals and sharing technical knowledge, this partnership helps us to strengthen universal health coverage, streamline regulatory systems, and build an interoperable, secure, and people-centred health ecosystem across Asean.
"As the Asean Co-Chair, Malaysia is committed to fostering a productive dialogue today. We look forward to adopting a Joint Statement that reflects our shared aspirations and provides clear direction for deeper collaboration in building a more connected, trusted and resilient regional health future," he said.
Meanwhile, ROK Vice Minister of Health and Welfare Lee Hyung Hoon, who co-chaired the meeting, said stronger digital health cooperation was crucial to bridging healthcare and digital gaps among Asean member states.
He said digital health had become a central pillar of Asean–ROK health cooperation since both sides agreed to establish a health dialogue channel at the 2019 Asean–ROK Commemorative Summit.
"Since then, we have strengthened human resource capacity in health and biotechnology while contributing to stronger regional health security surveillance through the Asean Biological Surveillance Centre (ABVC).
"The Asean-ROK Health Big Data Capacity Building Project, which begins this year, will serve as another launchpad for all member states to take their data capacity to the next level," he said.
He said the initiative would help member states strengthen their capacity to harness health data and digital technologies, while ensuring that the benefits of innovation were shared more equitably across the region.
Hyung Hoon added that the ROK had identified three key objectives to advance cooperation, including connecting existing digital health infrastructure to develop interoperable health information systems.
"The second is to cooperate on strengthening governance and workforce capacity so that AI can take root safely and equitably, regardless of varying levels of digital readiness.
"Third, to bring our discussions together under the Live Together AI-Powered Health and Society framework and give our future cooperation a clear architecture," he said.
He said the theme of the 17th AHMM, "Together Towards Equitable Future-Ready Health Systems," reflected Asean and the ROK's shared commitment to ensuring that digital transformation benefits communities across the region, regardless of differences in digital readiness and healthcare capacity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM: MA63 must be made a national narrative
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants discussions on the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) to be turned into a national narrative.
He said that he had previously proposed this approach, as current discussions remain largely sectoral and are held annually between the federal government and both states.
Anwar said that by transforming it into a national agenda, matters regarding the interests of Sabah and Sarawak would no longer be viewed merely as special considerations for the two states.
"I have suggested that MA63 discussions be framed as a national narrative. This is vital because otherwise, it remains sectoral, requiring special discussions for Sabah and Sarawak every year.
"It is a national commitment regarding development, stability, and the promises made during Malaya's independence in 1957 and Malaysia's formation in 1963. That must be sealed as a national narrative.
"We must encourage Malaysians not to speak only about their own race, party, or group, but to engage in a discourse that brings integrity and strength to the nation.
"I truly appreciate this, and we must make it clear that this is a national commitment and policy. For instance, when we increase allocations or Article 112D provisions to Sarawak and Sabah — in this context, Sabah — people in Peninsular Malaysia should not view this as special treatment for Sabah and Sarawak.
"So I hope this narrative is accepted in Peninsular Malaysia as well as in Sabah and Sarawak as a national policy, a national commitment, and a national narrative," he said at a press conference after chairing the MA63 Implementation Action Council (MTPMA63) meeting.
Also present were Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg, Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak Affairs) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud.
Meanwhile, addressing Sabah's claim to 40 per cent of net revenue, Anwar said that negotiations will continue while taking into account the financial position, as stipulated in the original agreement.
He said he had previously agreed to immediately increase the special grant starting this year to RM1.5 billion as an interim measure, with the funds to be disbursed in Oct or Nov.
"Negotiations are ongoing while taking into account the financial position as per the initial agreement. However, if the increase is too small, it might be disputed.
"So we are waiting for the parliamentary budget this October to present the paper and subsequently disburse the RM1.5 billion amount this year, likely by late October or early November," he said.
Earlier, Hajiji said that Sabah is requesting due consideration for the settlement of the 40 per cent revenue payment claimed by the state.
"We hope this issue can also be resolved and expedited. That is the position on behalf of the state of Sabah," Hajiji said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Private tutor charged with exposing 4-year-old to physical injury
Article:
AYER KEROH: A 25-year-old private tutor today pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here to a charge of exposing a 4-year-old girl under her care to physical injury last year.
Nur Dalila Salleh entered the plea after the charge was read before Judge Rohatul Akmar Abdullah.
She is accused of exposing the 4-year-old girl under her care to physical injury at a residence in Taman Belia Antarabangsa, at 1pm on Dec 12, 2025.
The charge was framed under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a fine of up to RM50,000, imprisonment for up to 20 years, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Qaiyyum Ramlan proposed bail at RM15,000 with additional conditions that the accused report to the nearest police station regularly and refrain from tampering with prosecution witnesses.
Defence counsel Norfazlinda Alimad pleaded for a lower bail, arguing that its sole purpose was to ensure attendance in court rather than serve as a punishment.
She added that the accused resides in Melaka, poses no flight risk, has no prior criminal record, and had fully cooperated throughout the police investigation.
The court heard that the accused is single, works as an e-commerce administrator earning RM1,700 a month, and supports her parents, including her mother who suffers from a knee nerve condition.
Judge Rohatul Akmar allowed bail at RM9,000 with one surety, alongside the prosecution's requested conditions. The accused posted bail.
The court fixed Oct 16 for mention and submission of documents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid's speech was that of a prime minister-in-waiting, says KJ
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Khairy Jamaluddin said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's policy speech showed that the party and Barisan Nasional were ready to form the next government.
The former Umno Youth chief went as far as describing Zahid's policy speech as "the speech of a prime minister-in-waiting".
"This is the speech of a prime minister-in-waiting, and a speech of a government-in-waiting," he said after Zahid delivered his presidential policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly today.
Former Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Hishammuddin Hussein said the party's experience over the past eight years showed that political fortunes could change, with Umno moving from a period of decline to one of recovery.
"I think the speech touched on the party's journey over the past eight years. The lessons from those eight years show that in politics there are cycles.
"There are times when we rise and times when we fall. When we rise, we are praised and supported.
"But when we fell over the past eight years, we were criticised, attacked and subjected to allegations," he said.
Both Hishammuddin and Khairy were among 6,252 former Umno leaders and members readmitted under the Rumah Bangsa initiative.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt seeks more ideas to power auto sector
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is seeking greater industry input on policies, incentives and fiscal measures for the 2027 Budget to strengthen Malaysia's automotive sector.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said the focus is on high-tech manufacturing, electric vehicles (EVs) and next-generation vehicles (NxGVs).
Amir Hamzah said the automotive industry is an important catalyst for economic growth, with the potential to raise its contribution to the the gross domestic product (GDP) while supporting the country's EV adoption targets.
He said strengthening the high-tech automotive sector could create more high-value jobs, enhance the country's export competitiveness and accelerate technology transfer and local talent development.
"The empowerment of the high-tech automotive sector is not only able to generate high-value employment opportunities and strengthen the country's export competitiveness, but also serve as a catalyst for technology transfer and the development of local human capital," he said in a statement.
Amir Hamzah led a 2027 Budget engagement session today in Tanjung Malim, Perak, with local and international automotive industry players.
The session, organised by the Finance Ministry in collaboration with the Northern Corridor Implementation Authority (NCIA) and hosted by DRB-HICOM Bhd, brought together industry players from the Automotive Hi-Tech Valley (AHTV).
Amir Hamzah said feedback from industry players would be important in reviewing policies, incentives and fiscal measures to be included under the 2027 Budget.
Among the key areas discussed were measures to improve productivity and attract foreign direct investment (FDI), while strengthening the sector's competitiveness in the region.
The government is also looking at supporting digitalisation, research and development (R&D), as well as the development of an ecosystem for EVs and new energy vehicles (NEVs).
Another priority is strengthening the domestic supply chain by enabling local vendors and suppliers to integrate more effectively into global value chains.
This would help increase domestic value-added and build the capabilities of Malaysian companies in technology and high-value manufacturing, the ministry said.
Human capital development was also highlighted, with greater emphasis on reskilling and upskilling workers to meet the requirements of future engineering and manufacturing activities.
The government expects the growth of a more productive and technology-intensive automotive industry to generate wider economic spillovers through higher-skilled employment, increased business activity, stronger exports and greater domestic value-added.
In the longer term, the expansion of economic activity could also strengthen the country's revenue base, it said.
The efforts are aligned with the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 and the National Automotive Policy 2020, which aim to position Malaysia as an Asean production and export hub for NxGVs and environmentally friendly vehicles.
Meanwhile, Amir Hamzah said the preparation of the 2027 Budget was being carried out through an inclusive engagement process involving state governments, industry, financial institutions, the business community and the wider public.
The government is also adopting an Outcome Based Budgeting approach, which focuses on the results generated by public spending.
"The approach aims to ensure that every ringgit spent solves the problems of the people, opens up economic opportunities and produces a tangible impact," he said.
He added that this was important to ensure government allocations were managed efficiently, with performance measured transparently and spending delivering the intended outcomes.
Feedback gathered during the Perak visit and other engagement sessions nationwide will be considered in finalising the 2027 Budget, which the government said would remain focused on inclusive and balanced development under the Ekonomi Madani framework.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid takes veiled swipe at Anwar over Budi95 quota flip-flop
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today took a veiled dig at Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over the government's flip-flopping Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) subsidised petrol quota.
Zahid said the government had reduced the monthly quota for the fuel earlier this year, only to restore it last month.
"When people are afraid, it is reinstated. Then it is withdrawn again, and near the election, it is reinstated again. Who does this? Guru," he said in his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Although Zahid did not name the leader, he is believed to have been referring to Anwar.
The reference to "Guru", or teacher in English, was linked to a leaked audio recording of a telephone conversation between Zahid and Anwar in April 2021, during which Zahid referred to Anwar as "Guru".
He said Umno was also not a party that promised to win today as though all problems would be resolved the following day."We are not a party that promises to win today... win today... (in jest) as though all the problems would be solved the very next day," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mondelez invests RM90mil to expand capacity at Cadbury plant in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Mondelez International's RM90 million investment in its Cadbury plant in Selangor will expand production capacity to meet growing demand in both Malaysia andexport markets, according to Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
The company's single largest investment at the Shah Alam confectionery plant was launched today with the completion of its new Crumb Tower.
Amirudin said the investment also reflects Mondelez's confidence in Selangor as a long-term manufacturing base.
"We can no longer be content with being consumers. We must move up the value chain and become producers of content and products that people in other countries want to consume.
"Mondelez's investment today is a testament to Selangor's commitment to providing a long-term home for small and medium enterprises as well as multinational companies that are confident in investing in new technologies and automation to improve worker productivity.
"The Crumb Tower is an example of how technology can transform food manufacturing," he said the launching event.
The investment comes as Mondelez seeks to strengthen the Shah Alam plant through greater automation, advanced process technology and improved operational efficiency, supporting Malaysia's position in high-value food manufacturing.
The Crumb Tower enables the plant to produce chocolate crumb locally, a key building block in chocolate production that was previously imported from markets including South Africa and Australia.
The move is expected to improve the plant's self-sufficiency, strengthen supply chain resilience and create additional capacity to support markets beyond Southeast Asia.
Mondelez International Malaysia and Singapore managing director Simon Crowther said the investment reflected the company's confidence in Malaysia and the capabilities developed at its Shah Alam operations over the past five decades.
"The Crumb Tower reflects our continued commitment to investing in Malaysia and strengthening our manufacturing capabilities through advanced technology and local expertise.
"By producing crumb locally, we are building greater self-sufficiency while positioning Shah Alam to play a larger role within our regional manufacturing network," he said.
The Crumb Tower integrates three advanced manufacturing systems.
They comprise a fully enclosed high-capacity powder handling system, a new-generation T-reactor — the first of its design in Malaysia — and an advanced fat handling system designed to rigorous process-safety standards.
The systems enable a highly automated and digitally controlled production process, while the facility was designed to meet international quality and food safety standards, including Halal requirements throughout the production process.
The investment also supports the development of Malaysian engineers and operators, who have been trained to manage the new systems, including process controls, data analysis and sophisticated equipment maintenance.
Local suppliers involved in the technology have also been qualified to support other Mondelez sites globally, extending the impact of the investment across Malaysia's manufacturing ecosystem.
Mondelez has maintained a manufacturing presence in Selangor for more than 50 years, with Cadbury products produced at the Shah Alam facility since 1974.
Crowther said the Shah Alam facility is positioned to play a larger role in Mondelez's regional manufacturing network.
It combines local production, advanced technology and Malaysian technical expertise to support both domestic and export markets.
Amirudin said the investment also reflects the state's push to attract companies that invest in technology and automation while creating higher-value employment opportunities.
He said Selangor was also working towards developing a stronger technical and vocational education and training ecosystem by 2030 to ensure its workforce could meet the changing needs of industries.
Selangor's economic activity exceeded RM460 billion in 2025 and is expected to surpass RM500 billion by 2027 or 2028, he said.

Title: AI firm Anthropic detects fake accounts targeting Malaysian voters for manipulation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia has been targeted in an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven commercial manipulation operation involving more than 1,000 fake X accounts, voter data and constituency-based targeting systems aimed at influencing political sentiment.
Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI platform, exposed the operation in a report after finding an account had used its platform for election manipulation targeting Malaysian users.
According to Anthropic's report, 'Detecting and Countering Misuse of AI: September 2026', published on its website, the platform was linked to an Istanbul-based technology company selling access to "influence-as-a-service" capabilities.
The report said the platform was built using Claude and marketed as a real-time, AI-powered political operations ecosystem.
It was used to profile and target Malaysian voters by parliamentary constituency using census and election data.
The operation also managed about 1,000 fake X accounts optimised to boost engagement while evading detection by the platform.
The system was allegedly equipped with fake news websites using AI-powered rewriting tools to generate content.
The report alleged that the operation used real census data and millions of voter records to target Malaysia's most sensitive political and social fault lines, including race, religion and the royal institution, across all 222 parliamentary constituencies.
The platform was allegedly capable of setting the number of artificial views for a target, including one request to generate one million fake views.
The report stressed, however, that the figures were based on internal records and could not be independently verified.
Anthropic said it detected and removed the accounts following an internal investigation. It also used the identified indicators to map the wider operational network and disrupt similar misuse in future.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia Day celebration to showcase unity, harmony across regions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Day 2026 celebration, scheduled to be held at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK), Sarawak on Sept 16, will reflect the harmony and togetherness of Malaysians across the regions through the diversity of cultures and shared beliefs.
Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah said the uniqueness of this year's celebration would highlight the spirit of Segulai Sejalai (togetherness) through the unity of various races in a national-level official event.
He said this manifestation of harmony would be showcased through the Majlis Kesyukuran involving various faiths organised by the Unit for Other Religions (UNIFOR) on Sept 14, which would demonstrate unity among followers of various religions.
"This majlis kesyukuran is being held together with people of different faiths, who are also contributing according to their respective beliefs to ensure that the ceremony is conducted smoothly," he said when he appeared as a guest on the Apa Khabar Malaysia programme produced by Bernama TV today.
Halim said this would be followed by a thanksgiving event by Muslims at the State Mosque on Sept 15, which would be graced by Sarawak Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Dr Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar.
Halim said the highlight of the Malaysia Day celebration would also feature local traditions through a symbolic cutting of pulut kuning instead of the traditional cake-cutting ceremony, as well as the signing of the Malaysia Proclamation Book by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor to commemorate the physical and spiritual unity of all Malaysians.
He said the event would also be enlivened by a combination of silat, hadrah, gendang pampat drumming, lion dance, a theatre performance depicting the formation of Malaysia, as well as a concert featuring local artistes, in addition to a fireworks display at the Kuching Waterfront.
He also invited all Malaysians to watch the live broadcast of the celebration on RTM TV1 and TVS, as well as special coverage by Bernama.
"I am confident that Malaysians are eagerly looking forward to the 2026 celebration becoming a reality because although the weather may pose some challenges, we have made every effort to ensure its success.
"May, with Allah's permission, everything proceed smoothly, and we can celebrate in a peaceful and harmonious atmosphere, with everything successfully carried out," he said.
This year's celebration retains the National Day theme 'Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati', paired with Sarawak's unity slogan Segulai Sejalai.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Straits Energy to tighten grip on US-listed TMD Energy with 96pct voting control
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Straits Energy Resources Bhd is seeking to tighten its grip on US-listed subsidiary TMD Energy Ltd, with a proposed dual-class share structure set to raise its voting power to nearly 100 per cent.
Straits Energy's equity stake in TMD Energy will remain unchanged at 65.08 per cent, giving it significantly greater voting control without increasing its ownership.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, Straits Energy said TMD Energy proposed to split its existing ordinary shares into Class A and Class B shares.
Each Class A share will carry one vote, while each Class B share will carry 20 votes. Both classes will have the same rights to dividends and distributions.
Under the exercise, 10 million TMD Energy shares held by Straits Energy will be converted into Class B shares on a one-for-one basis, while all other issued shares will become Class A shares.
Straits Energy will also hold another 5.34 million Class A shares.
This will give the company about 205.34 million votes, or 96.15 per cent of the total.
Public shareholders, who collectively own 17.71 per cent of TMD Energy, will hold about 1.95 per cent of the voting rights following the exercise.
Straits Energy said the dual-class structure would allow it to retain control over TMD Energy and determine its strategic direction even if the NYSE American-listed company issues more Class A shares in future.
Such shares could be issued to raise funds, for employee incentive schemes, acquisitions or other corporate purposes.
The structure would therefore give TMD Energy greater flexibility to raise money from external investors without diluting Straits Energy's voting control.
The exercise will not involve any new shares, cash payment or capital outlay, and will not immediately dilute the economic interests of existing shareholders.
Straits Energy said it did not expect the exercise to have any material effect on its earnings per share, net assets per share or gearing.
The proposal is subject to approval from TMD Energy shareholders at its annual general meeting on Oct 7, as well as any other regulatory or third-party approvals required.
Straits Energy expects the exercise to be completed by the fourth quarter of 2026.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UMS professor acquitted of 21 false claims charges
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A university professor walked free from the Special Corruption Court today after being acquitted on 21 charges of making false claims for research funds related to Sabah's marine life.
Sessions Court Judge Jason Juga discharged and acquitted Prof Dr Charles Santhanaraju Vairappan after finding that the prosecution had failed to prove a prima facie case against him on all the charges under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009.
In arriving at the decision, Jason found that the prosecution had failed to establish the ingredients of the charges.
"In evaluating the evidence presented before the court during the prosecution's case, based on the prevailing facts, I found that there are doubts in the evidence presented which render the charges unproven, that the accused had submitted documents which he had reason to believe contained false material particulars with intent to deceive his principal, as set out in the charges," he said.
The court also ordered the bail deposit to be refunded and the accused's passport returned.
Charles claimed trial to all 21 charges on July 20, 2022.
He was accused of submitting claim documents, namely official receipts containing false details, to officers at the Jabatan Bendahari Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) between May 2014 and April 2017, with the intention of deceiving his principal.
The receipts stated payments of between RM300 and RM5,550, totalling RM66,190, for diving activities, boat charters to several islands and van charters, among others, when in fact there had been no such expenditure.
He was charged under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, punishable under Section 24(2) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum 20-year jail term and a fine of five times the amount involved or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.
The prosecution called 26 witnesses during the hearing.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Rustam Sanip of the MACC appeared for the prosecution, while lawyers Zahir Shah, Baldev Singh and Kelvin Wong represented the accused.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Driver charged with murder over 11-vehicle crash that killed four
Article:
TEMERLOH: A lorry driver was charged with
murdering
four people in an 11-vehicle crash along the East Coast Expressway on the night of Aug 31.
The charge against Zulkarnain Md Noh, 52, was read out before Magistrate Nuur Fakhizaa Abu Bakar during a court proceeding held at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah.
No plea was recorded.
Zulkarnain was charged with the murders of Muhammad Nazatullah Nazmi, 32, his wife Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, their son, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef, 4, and Seow Beng Wai, 55.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, with at least 12 strokes of the rotan, upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutors Najimi Arif Nasarudin and Anis Syakilla Zawawi prosecuted.
The court set Nov 12 for mention.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Baja 3 probe: Mat Sabu says yet to be called in by MACC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu has not been called in by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to assist in investigations into alleged delays in the supply of Additional Padi Compound Fertiliser 3 (Baja 3) to farmers in Kedah.
Mohamad said he and the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry were ready to give their cooperation to the authorities if required.
"So far, I have not been called in. If required, the ministry and I are ready to give our full cooperation to the authorities," he said when contacted today.
He said the ministry would leave it entirely to the authorities to conduct the investigation and ensure that all matters related to the issue were thoroughly examined.
"There is nothing to hide and we are open to assisting with any investigation," he said.
Earlier, MACC said it was prepared to call in the minister and the ministry's secretary-general if necessary to assist in investigations into alleged delays in the distribution of Baja 3 to about 60,000 padi farmers in Kedah.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman was reported to have said that instructions had been issued for a comprehensive investigation to be conducted, covering all parties linked to the policy, implementation and tender process for the supply of the fertiliser.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/1529922/updated-padi-fertiliser-probe-macc-may-call-minister-senior-officials
He said 13 witnesses had so far been called in and their statements recorded, comprising the chairman of the Malaysian Padi Farmers Brotherhood Organisation (PeSAWAH), four officials from the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada) and eight staff members of Area Farmers' Organisations.
The complaint was lodged on Aug 26 following allegations of failure by the appointed supplier, TaaVeeKun Manufacturing Sdn Bhd (Taaveekun), to supply, deliver and distribute Baja Padi 3 under the Padi Production Incentive Scheme (SIPP) in the Mada area.
The supply covers 100,000ha for the Season 1 and Season 2 crops this year over a one-year period, involving about 60,000 padi farmers.

Title: Anwar to announce interim payment for Sarawak on Malaysia Day
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is set to announce an interim payment to Sarawak related to the Malaysia Agreement 1963 on Malaysia Day, Sept 16.
Anwar said discussions on the matter with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg would continue over the next few days.
He said similar steps taken for Sabah would be considered for Sarawak, although the state is not covered under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution.
"Regarding Sarawak, I think although it is not included under the 112D constitutional provision, the same spirit should be considered.
"So I will continue discussions over these few days with the Premier, and hopefully by Malaysia Day on Sept 16 in Kuching, I can also announce an interim measure for Sarawak," he told a press conference after chairing a Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council meeting.
Abang Johari, Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor and Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud were involved in the meeting.
The prime minister previously announced a special interim payment of RM1.5 billion to Sabah until negotiations over the state's 40 per cent net revenue claim are resolved.
Anwar said Sarawak had also presented its views on a formula that could be introduced for special payments to Sabah and Sarawak.
"This is so that the formula clearly takes into account the country's financial position and capability, including what minimum and maximum limits can be considered.
"I agree and have asked the Finance Ministry and the Sarawak Finance Ministry to discuss introducing this formula," he said.
Commenting on the matter, Abang Johari said the formula proposed by Sarawak was a win-win approach for both parties.
"If our country prospers, the federation naturally benefits. If times are tough, we accept the reality to ensure the country's financial stability remains intact," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: GTA Holdings seals Brunei expansion with Safran Helicopter Engines distributorship
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: GTA Holdings Bhd has formalised its expansion into Brunei after securing a distributorship for selected Safran Helicopter Engines products and services in the neighbouring country.
This follows plans first announced in July, when GTA's subsidiary signed a memorandum of understanding with Safran Helicopter Engines Asia to expand their partnership beyond Malaysia into Brunei.
At the time, the proposed expansion was subject to approvals and the signing of definitive agreements.
The company today said its wholly-owned unit, Global Turbine Asia Sdn Bhd, had signed a distributor agreement with Safran Helicopter Engines Asia.
Under the agreement, GTA is authorised to market and support selected Safran helicopter engine products and services in Brunei.
GTA managing director and chief executive officer Datuk Nonee Ashirin Mohd Radzi said the appointment reflected Safran's confidence in the company following years of collaboration.
"This appointment is particularly meaningful as it reflects the confidence Safran Helicopter Engines Asia has placed in GTA after years of close collaboration and partnership.
"It is a testament to our team's technical capabilities, operational standards and commitment to supporting customers across the region," she said in a statement.
Nonee said the agreement would also strengthen GTA's presence in Brunei and deepen its relationship with Safran.
"Together, we share a common commitment to delivering reliable aerospace support solutions and strengthening aviation capabilities within the region," she added.
GTA is involved in maintenance, repair and overhaul services for helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft engines, parts and components.
Its operations are based at the Helicopter Centre at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang, serving aviation operators, maintenance and repair customers and defence-related markets.
Safran Helicopter Engines Asia, based in Singapore, supports more than 200 operators and over 1,100 helicopter engines across 19 countries in Asia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia sees continued volcanic activity, multiple eruptions recorded
Article:
JAKARTA: Multiple volcanic eruptions were recorded across Indonesia on Friday, with Mount Ili Lewotolok erupting six times and sending ash as high as 700m above its summit, while Mount Semeru and Mount Ibu also remained active.
The Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation Centre (PVMBG) said Ili Lewotolok in East Nusa Tenggara, which remains at Level II in Indonesia's four-tier volcano alert system, recorded the eruptions between 12.57am and 9.06am local time.
The latest eruption produced a thick grey ash column reaching about 700m above the summit and drifting westward, while earlier eruptions sent ash between 500m and 600m above the summit towards the west and northwest, according to data published on the centre's website.
Mount Semeru in East Java, which remains at Level III, the second-highest alert level, erupted four times between 12.26am and 6.16am, while Mount Ibu in North Maluku, which remains at Level II, recorded three eruptions between 12.49am and 8.58am, according to the data.
Meanwhile, the Geological Agency said Anak Krakatau in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra remained at Level III and continued to show volcanic activity following the end of its roughly 25-hour continuous eruption.
"The volcano's activity has shown an overall declining trend, although the probability of further eruptions remains high," the agency said in its latest social media post, adding that a 3km exclusion zone around the active crater remains in place.
Meanwhile, the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) said satellite imagery detected no volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau or Mount Ibu, although cloud cover could obscure observations.
In a separate development, the Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park authority said part of the Mount Bromo tourism area in East Java had been closed from Thursday until further notice following a fire at Savana Pengol as firefighting operations continued.
The authority said in a statement that the Jemplang entrance in Malang was closed to visitors, while tourists could still enter through Cemoro Lawang in Probolinggo and Wonokitri in Pasuruan, with access limited to the Sea of Sand and Watangan Savannah.
It said the Malang-Lumajang transport route remained open, while visitors were urged to stay away from the affected area and avoid activities that could trigger new fires.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man found dead in drain near SMK Tun Hussein Onn in Prai
Article:
PRAI: The body of a 37-year-old man was found in a 1.5m-deep drain near SMK Tun Hussein Onn here today.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said firefighters received a request from police at 12.10pm to recover the body.
He said a team from the Prai Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene and found the victim in the drain.
"Five firefighters recovered the body and handed it over to police."
The operation ended at 12.47pm.
Photos of the incident have since gone viral on social media.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: HE Group outlook brightens on data centre, semiconductor growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: HE Group Bhd's outlook remains positive underpinned by its strong data centre (DC) tender pipeline and growing semiconductor sector involvement, said Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest).
HE Group's wholly-owned subsidiary Hexatech Engineering SB accepted a purchase order worth RM25 million for power distribution system works for a manufacturer involved in assembling, testing and packing NAND flash memory products.
The project starts upon acceptance and is targeted for completion within 20 weeks (end of Jan 2027).
"This lifts HE Group's outstanding orderbook to about RM317.3 million, while its tenderbook stands at about RM1 billion (80 per cent DC-related)."
PublicInvest raised its financial year (FY26) orderbook replenishment target to RM430 million and revised up its FY27 to FY28 earnings forecasts by an average of 30 per cent, reflecting consistent tenderbook conversion.
The firm said HE Group's RM317.3 million outstanding orderbook and robust RM1 billion tenderbook provide earnings visibility in the near to medium term.
The firm said continued investments in DC and semiconductor infrastructure play directly to HE Group's expertise in electrical engineering, positioning the company well to capture further contract wins.
"Talent retention and copper price volatility remain key watchpoints, though management continues to actively manage both exposures.
"We upgrade our call on HE Group from Neutral to Outperform, with a higher target price of RM1.26 from 91 sen previously," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ku Li calls on ex-Umno members to return, strengthen party
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno veteran Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah has welcomed calls for former members to return to the party, saying Umno needs a "big family" to pool ideas to address challenges facing the Malay community.
Tengku Razaleigh, better known as Ku Li, said those who had left the party should be welcomed back as Umno needed their contributions and experience.
"They should come back. We welcome all of them to return to Umno. We want one big family.
"There are many responsibilities that we have to carry and we need more energy and ideas to solve the problems facing the ummah," he told reporters after attending the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
He also welcomed Pas representatives at the assembly, saying it could pave the way for the two parties to rebuild ties.
"It is good. I think it is good. We can unite again," he said.
He described the development as an encouraging sign for greater cooperation and unity among Malay political parties.
His remarks came as Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said 45,808 people had rejoined the party since the Rumah Bangsa concept was introduced about seven months ago.
Asyraf said the figure comprised former members who had rejoined Umno, reactivated their membership or joined the party through the initiative.
"This brings Umno's total membership as at Aug 31 to 3,251,456. By breakdown, Wanita Umno now has 1.4 million members, Youth has 418,000 and Puteri has 226,000," he said when presenting his report at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said in March that the party was opening its doors to former members to return without conditions.
Under the Rumah Bangsa initiative, everyone is welcome, with a committee formed to manage applications to join or rejoin the party, whether from individuals or blocs.
Among those who have since returned to Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) is former Bersatu Supreme Council member Tan Sri Noh Omar.
Two other veteran Umno and BN figures, Tan Sri Syed Hamid Albar and Datuk Seri Hishammuddin Tun Hussein, have also returned.
Their return was announced during the launch of the Johor BN election machinery.
Also present at the 2026 Umno General Assembly were MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, MIC president Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran, Pas vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad, Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, Pas information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari, Pas president's political secretary Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman, and Parti Progresif Penduduk (PPP) president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM2.4b drug lab: Police hunt 4 to 5 more suspects
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are hunting four to five more syndicate members linked to the RM2.4 billion drug laboratory busted recently, with some believed to have fled the country.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigators had identified the suspects and efforts were underway to track them down.
"We have identified them and we will find them. It is only a matter of time before we locate them," he told the New Straits Times today.
Hussein, however, declined to disclose the countries the suspects were believed to have fled to.
He said police were looking for between four and five people, all of whom had previous involvement in drug-related activities.
The hunt follows investigations into the syndicate linked to the large-scale drug laboratory, where drugs worth an estimated RM2.4 billion were uncovered.
It was reported that the drug laboratory located at Puncak Alam was believed to have been churning out billions of ringgit worth of drugs.
The operation came crashing down on Aug 15 when the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) raided the premises as part of Op Eumenes,
seizing more than 13 tonnes of liquid and powdered MDMA and other drugs estimated to be worth a staggering RM2.4 billion
.
The raid was part of six simultaneous and follow-up raids conducted around Selangor and Kuala Lumpur following intelligence and surveillance on the syndicate.
It was also reported that the man shot dead by police during a recent anti-drug operation in Seremban is
believed to have been the mastermind
behind the drug laboratory.
Investigations showed that the man headed the syndicate operating the clandestine laboratory.
He was responsible for bringing in equipment from overseas and recruiting other syndicate members.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman injured as car hits raised road fixture, overturns in PJ
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 46-year-old woman escaped with injuries after her Honda City overturned after hitting a raised metal fixture on the road in Petaling Jaya this morning.
Federal police Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) said the incident occurred at about 7.10am along Jalan Gasing-Jalan Templer, in front of a BHP petrol station.
"Initial investigations found that the vehicle's left tyre ran over a raised fixture, causing the underside of the vehicle to hit the metal before the driver lost control and the car overturned.
"The driver sustained injuries to her right leg from broken glass and was taken to Assunta Hospital for treatment," it said in a statement.
The department said preliminary investigations found that the accident was caused by the poorly maintained road fixture, which resulted in the driver losing control of the vehicle.
The vehicle was taken to the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters TEID.
The case was classified under Rule 10 of the Road Traffic Rules 166/59 for failing to exercise due control over vehicle movement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DNA results for five Long Lellang crash victims due by tomorrow, say Sarawak police
Article:
MIRI, Sept 11 — The deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) analysis for all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday is expected to be completed by tomorrow at the latest.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the remains would only be handed over to the respective next-of-kin once the DNA analysis was completed.
“We anticipate that the DNA analysis for the five victims could be completed by tomorrow at the latest,” he told reporters here today.
Earlier, post-mortem examinations on all five victims were completed at the hospital’s forensic department, with severe burn injuries identified as the cause of death.
Last Tuesday, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.
The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — Bernama

Title: Newborn’s body found in Dungun hostel locker, police investigating
Article:
DUNGUN, Sept 11 — A 19-year-old student allegedly hid her newborn baby’s body in a hostel locker after giving birth in a toilet at an educational institution here two days ago.
Dungun district police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received a report on the discovery of the body at 10.48pm yesterday.
He said the baby, believed to have been born at eight months’ gestation, was suspected to have died after birth.
Investigations found that the student allegedly wrapped the baby in cloth, placed the body in a bag, and kept it in a hostel locker.
“The matter came to light after the management of a mosque contacted the institution and informed them that the student had sought help to arrange the baby’s burial,” he said when contacted today.
Nik Ab Halim said police had recorded statements from several witnesses and examined the scene with assistance from the Forensic Unit.
The baby’s body was taken to Dungun Hospital for post-mortem and the case is being investigated under Section 318 of the Penal Code for concealment of birth. — Bernama

Title: Selangor sets Oct 26 as replacement holiday for Sultan’s Silver Jubilee
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 11 — Selangor has declared October 25 a special public holiday to commemorate the silver jubilee of Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah’s reign.
State Secretary Datuk Dr Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin said the holiday would be replaced on October 26 as the anniversary falls on a Sunday,
The Star
reported.
“Since the date falls on a Sunday, the following day, October 26 (Monday) is designated as the replacement public holiday,” he said during a press conference announcing details of the celebration.
He added that the holiday would be observed in the same way as the September 1 public holiday marking Selangor’s overall victory at Sukma 2026.
The September 1 holiday applied to all federal and state civil servants serving in Selangor, while private sector employers were encouraged to grant leave at their discretion.
Ahmad Fadzli said the jubilee celebration would feature around 20 programmes and official events, scheduled between September 28 and November 1.
The full list of events will be published on the social media platforms of the Selangor State Secretary’s Office.

Title: Was bad weather to blame? Investigators dig into what brought down deadly Long Lellang chopper
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau has begun its investigation into the cause of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang which claimed five lives, said Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah.
Hasbi said the ministry’s air accident investigation team was already at the crash site and was working to determine the cause of the tragedy.
“We will wait for the report from the Air Accident Investigation Team. We cannot say anything at this stage,” he said when met by reporters after launching the National Madani Taxi Renewal Programme here on Friday.
Asked if bad weather could have caused the crash, Hasbi said it was too early to draw any conclusions.
“We will wait for the report. I cannot predict it because everything will depend on the investigation, including the weather,” he said, adding that the report was expected to be completed soon.
The BO-105 helicopter, registered 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing airport in Ulu Baram while conducting an FDS mission on Sept 8.
All five crew members, including the pilot, on board, were killed in the crash. They were identified as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — The Borneo Post

Title: Tanker driver, still hospitalised, charged with murder over Pahang crash that wiped out young family on Merdeka Day
Article:
TEMERLOH, Sept 11 — A cement tanker driver receiving treatment at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah was charged today with four counts of murder over a crash that killed four people on Aug 31.
No plea was recorded from the accused, Zulkarnain Md Noh, 52, after the charges were read before Magistrate Nuur Fakhizaa Abu Bakar, as the case falls under the High Court’s jurisdiction.
Zulkarnain is accused of having caused the deaths of Muhammad Nazatullah Nazmi, Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef Muhammad Nazatullah and Seow Beng Wai.
The offences were allegedly committed at about 10.30pm on Aug 31 at KM110.3 of the East Coast Expressway (LPT) eastbound.
He was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code (Act 574), which carries the death penalty, or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and not less than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutors Najimi Arif Nasarudin and Anis Syakilla Zawawi appeared for the prosecution, while the accused was unrepresented.
Magistrate Nuur Fakhizaa set Nov 12 for document submission and mention.
On Sept 1, four people were killed after a cement-laden tanker was believed to have lost control and crashed into several other vehicles that were moving slowly at the location.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob was reported to have said the three victims travelling in a Proton S70 were a married couple, Muhammad Nazatullah and Nur Atiqah Sofiya, and their son, while Seow Beng Wai was a passenger in a Honda CR-V.
He said Seow’s son, Sebastian Seow Jhen, 18, who was driving the Honda CR-V, and the tanker driver sustained serious injuries and were treated at Hospital Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah in Temerloh.
The drivers and passengers of eight other vehicles, including an express bus, a Toyota Hilux, a Toyota Alphard and five other cars, suffered minor injuries. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar visits Kampung Numbak fire victims, pledges aid
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited and offered support to victims of the Kampung Numbak fire at the temporary relief centre at the Damai Multipurpose Hall here today.
Anwar, accompanied by Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor, arrived at the relief centre at 1.30 pm and spent about 20 minutes meeting the victims.
The Prime Minister was then briefed on the fire by Kota Kinabalu Mayor Datuk Seri Dr Sabin Samitah before handing over aid to the victims.
A total of 111 heads of household received food baskets as well as RM1,500 in special financial assistance from the federal government.
Earlier, Anwar and Hajiji joined more than 100 residents for Friday prayers at the nearby Masjid Jamek Kampung Likas.
One of the victims, Ruhin Nya Amrani, 52, said the assistance is a great help, particularly in covering the expenses of her two children, who are in secondary school.
“I am touched that the Prime Minister himself came to visit us and provide assistance. This will certainly help ease our burden,” she said.
Mohd Jamri Jamjiru, 43, said the government’s assistance will be put to good use.
“We appreciate all the assistance given, but what matters now is for the government to speed up efforts to rebuild our settlement,” he said.
The Kampung Numbak fire on Aug 30 destroyed about 200 houses built over the water, killing three people. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Umno proposing ‘Grand Collaboration’ to end political clashes in Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — A proposal for the formation of a “Grand Collaboration” through political understanding (Tafahum Siyasi) among the country’s political party coalitions has been put forward to avoid political clashes that would be detrimental to the ummah and the nation, said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
He said the concept does not involve a merger of political parties, but rather a common ground for mutual understanding aimed at preserving political stability and reinvigorating national economic growth.
He said the approach draws lessons from the wisdom of the Treaty of Hudaibiyah and the opening of Makkah, which demonstrated that political victory and understanding must be accompanied by the values of forgiveness, compassion and unity.
“This Grand Collaboration is not a merger of parties. Instead, it is an understanding aimed at avoiding clashes that would be detrimental. I understand and can sense the concerns of the Malays, who no longer want us to clash and quarrel among ourselves.
“However, in building this common ground, we are not forcing any party to dilute its identity. In other words, whoever Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) work with, Umno remains Umno, and Barisan Nasional remains Barisan Nasional,” he said.
He said this when delivering his presidential address at the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre (WTC) here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Deputy Prime Minister, outlined three key principles in guiding the Tafahum Siyasi understanding: prioritising common ground for the benefit of the ummah, respecting differences in ideology as well as the respective parties’ guidelines, and upholding the principle of flexibility in practising tolerance.
He also stressed that honesty and sincerity are key prerequisites that cannot be compromised in making the political understanding a success, in order to prevent a repeat of episodes of betrayal and broken agreements.
At the same time, Ahmad Zahid said Umno needs to remember its fundamental character as a party that does not merely think superficially from one election cycle to another, but is capable of planning the nation’s development with a long-term vision spanning generations.
According to Ahmad Zahid, the party’s struggle has always been underpinned by its ability to formulate inclusive socioeconomic plans for the well-being of the people and the nation.
He cited the introduction of the New Economic Policy (NEP) and the National Transformation 2050 (TN50) vision as examples of the party’s commitment to addressing the aspirations of new generations, including Gen Z and Gen Alpha.
“We need to remember Umno’s true character. We do not think only from one election term to the next. The reality is that Umno is a party that has always planned the nation’s development across generations.
“The NEP, for example, was not formulated to win applause for a season. TN50 was conceived to address the thinking and aspirations of Gen Z through to Gen Alpha. That is how a governing party thinks,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid said the party’s priority is not merely to win a series of elections, but to ensure that a strong national framework and direction can be passed on to the next generation of leaders. — Bernama

Title: Sabah gets RM1.5b MA63 boost, Anwar hints Sarawak could be next by Sept 16
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The interim allocation for Sabah will immediately rise to RM1.5 billion this year, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said this in reply to a request from Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor during the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Council meeting (MTPMA63) press conference here.
Anwar pointed out the payment is an interim measure and that negotiations would continue, taking into account the country’s financial position, as provided for in the original agreement.
