“However, if the increase is too small, it may be disputed. So, we will wait for Parliament in October to table the paper and then disburse the RM1.5 billion this year as well, perhaps at the end of October or early November,” he stated.
Hajiji had earlier, on behalf of the Sabah state government, also requested the settlement of the 40 per cent payment to Sabah.
“Therefore, we hope that this matter can also be resolved and expedited. That is on behalf of the Sabah government,” said Hajiji.
Separately, Anwar also said for Sarawak, although it is not included under Article 112D of the Federal Constitution, the same spirit should nevertheless be taken into consideration.
“Therefore, I will continue discussions with the Premier over the next few days. Hopefully, by 16th September, Malaysia Day in Kuching, I will also be able to announce an interim measure for Sarawak,” he said.
He added that Sarawak has also put forward its views on a formula that should be introduced, so that the formula clearly takes into account the country’s financial position and capacity, as well as the minimum that can be considered and the maximum.
“I agree and I have asked the Ministry of Finance and the Sarawak Ministry of Finance to discuss the introduction of such a formula,” said Anwar.
Sarawak Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg expressed his appreciation for the earlier discussion and for the decisions that have been reached. — The Borneo Post

Title: Perak orders caterer at Lenggong boarding school to shut after almost 160 students, staff fall sick
Article:
IPOH, September 11 — A food caterer serving a boarding school in Lenggong, Perak has been ordered to close after 159 students and staff developed symptoms of suspected food poisoning.
Perak Health, Human Resources, Indian Affairs and National Integration Committee chairman Datuk A. Sivanesan said the Hulu Perak District Health Office received a report of the incident from Lenggong Health Clinic on September 10.
He said those affected, aged between 13 and 52, began developing symptoms from 11.30pm on September 9, with the latest case reported at 1.40pm the following day.
“Of the 159 cases, all experienced diarrhoea and abdominal pain, while 125 had headaches, 89 had nausea, 31 had vomiting and 15 had fever,” he said in a statement today.
All were treated by a medical team at the school, with 10 receiving further treatment at Lenggong Health Clinic, while none required hospitalisation and all remained stable.
Sivanesan said 34 clinical samples, 14 environmental samples and one food sample were collected and sent to the Ipoh Public Health Laboratory for analysis.
He said the suspected food was supplied for a programme at the school on September 9 by an external caterer engaged by the programme organiser.
The Hulu Perak District Health Office inspected the caterer’s premises at 2pm on September 10 and recorded a score of 78.16 per cent.
“Following the inspection, the food premises were ordered to close under Section 18(1)(d) of the Prevention and Control of Infectious Diseases Act 1988,” he said.
The operator was also ordered to clean the premises, carry out corrective measures and conduct regular pest control, while the school dining hall continued operating as usual.
Sivanesan also urged food handlers to comply with the Food Act 1983 and Food Hygiene Regulations 2009 to prevent further food poisoning incidents.

Title: Sounds like a ‘PM in waiting’, Khairy says of Zahid’s speech at Umno assembly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s keynote at the party’s general assembly this morning earned praise from Khairy Jamaluddin.
Khairy, an Umno returnee after being sacked three years ago for alleged disciplinary infractions and breaches of party discipline during GE15 – described the speech as crystal clear on Barisan Nasional’s (BN) direction ahead of the coming general election.
“This is the speech of a prime minister in waiting and a speech of a government in waiting,” Khairy told reporters after Zahid’s speech at the 2026 Umno general assembly here.
In his address, Zahid described Umno as a far-sighted party with a long-term vision for Malaysia, rather than one that merely hopes to survive one election after another.
He also called for the GE16 to be held as soon as possible, saying it was time for BN to seek a fresh mandate to lead the country.
Zahid further pledged that Malaysia’s courts and institutions would not be used as political tools should BN return to Putrajaya.
The third day of the assembly was also attended by four PAS leaders, including its vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad, secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari, and assistant secretary-general Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman.

Title: DNA tests pending for five victims of Long Lellang helicopter crash, says Sarawak police
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 11 — The post-mortems on all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service helicopter crash in Long Lellang last Tuesday were completed at 7.30pm yesterday.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said the cause of death for all five victims was severe burn injuries sustained in the helicopter crash.
“For now, we are awaiting the results of the deoxyribonucleic acid samples for scientific confirmation,” he told Bernama.
On Tuesday, the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia said a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals, including the pilot, had crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Airport.
The victims were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and two nurses, Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44. — Bernama

Title: No U-turn: Ex-minister Dr Zaliha says she has backed Health Service Commission proposal since 2023
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Former Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa today denied making a U-turn on the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission, saying she had remained committed to the initiative since 2023.
She said a report by a health portal yesterday, which claimed she had reversed her stance, was inaccurate and did not reflect the full context, stressing that efforts on the matter had continued throughout her tenure at the Ministry of Health (MOH).
In a statement, Dr Zaliha said that as early as February 2023, she had publicly stated that the proposal to establish the commission was among the key matters being considered in the final draft of the Health White Paper.
“In fact, in April 2023, the same news portal reported on my meeting with representatives of Hartal Doktor Kontrak (HDK), where the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission and a Health Reform Commission was discussed within the framework of the White Paper,” she said.
On her parliamentary reply on June 15, 2023, which she said had often been misinterpreted, Dr Zaliha explained that it was a clarification on the scope of authority of a Service Commission under Article 144 of the Federal Constitution.
She said the functions of a Service Commission cover appointments, confirmation of service, promotions, transfers and disciplinary action, but establishing such a commission does not give it the power to create new posts or formulate remuneration systems, including setting more competitive emolument rates.
“I also explained that establishing a new Service Commission would involve a complex process, including the need to amend the Federal Constitution and secure a two-thirds majority in both the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara.
“That explanation was about the structure, jurisdiction and limitations of the model available at the time, and was not an outright rejection of the proposal to establish a Health Service Commission,” she said.
Dr Zaliha cited records after the July 2023 parliamentary session showing that she had publicly confirmed the Government’s intention to establish the commission and was assessing the best model for it.
She said the commitment was followed by the establishment of a Technical Working Group by the MOH in October 2023 to identify the best methods and mechanisms for setting up the Health Service Commission.
Dr Zaliha reiterated that her position on the welfare of healthcare workers had remained unchanged, stressing that any reform of the healthcare service system, including the establishment of the commission, must be implemented urgently and backed by an authority capable of resolving the crises faced by healthcare personnel.
According to media reports yesterday, Dr Zaliha called for the Government to expedite the establishment of the commission following the helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, but the news portal in question described the call as a “U-turn”. — Bernama

Title: From complaint to compensation: How victims in Malaysia are winning sexual harassment cases
Article:
SEMPORNA, Sept 11 — The Sexual Harassment Tribunal Agency (Tags) under the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) recorded 134 sexual harassment complaints over a two-year period, with 90 of them successfully resolved.
Its Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the figures showed that Tags, which was established on March 8, 2024, played an important role as a main avenue for helping victims seek resolution and redress for the incidents they experienced.
“The figure only covers complaints received at KPWKM counters and does not include police reports. Male victims and children can also use this platform to seek redress. So far this year, four male victims have filed cases with the tribunal.
“Some victims have also won their cases and received compensation,” she told reporters after officiating the Semporna Zero Tolerance for Violence: Advocacy Against Sexual Harassment and End Violence Against Women programmes here yesterday.
She said KPWKM continued to provide support through advocacy, education and the provision of easily accessible assistance channels so that victims would not continue to remain silent when faced with sexual harassment.
Elaborating on the domestic violence statistics, Nancy said 4,646 cases had been reported nationwide up to July this year, including 424 cases in Sabah.
“The figures show that women’s safety requires more comprehensive, integrated and sustained action through a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach,” she said.
In addition, Nancy advised victims of violence or sexual harassment to have the courage to speak up through the proper channels and to keep evidence that could assist in the process of seeking redress. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: KPWKM are the Malay initials for the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development.

Title: Anwar: Time to make MA63 part of the national conversation, not just Sabah-Sarawak issue
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) to become part of the national narrative rather than being viewed solely as an issue concerning Sabah and Sarawak.
He said the approach was important to ensure Malaysians understood that the government’s commitment to MA63 formed part of the Madani Government’s national policy and was closely linked to the country’s development, stability and unity.
Anwar said this must be understood and embraced by people in peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak as part of a national policy, commitment and narrative aimed at strengthening the country.
“I have proposed that discussions on MA63 be made part of the national narrative. It is very important because otherwise, it becomes a sectoral issue.
“Every year, we have to hold separate discussions on Sabah and Sarawak. No. This is a national commitment about development, stability, and what we promised when Malaysia was formed.
“This must be firmly established as a national narrative. We need to encourage Malaysians not to speak only about their race, party or group, but to engage in a broader discourse that strengthens the nation,” he told a press conference after chairing the 2026 Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council meeting at the Sabah International Convention Centre here today.
Also present were Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
The Prime Minister said people in peninsular Malaysia should also not view additional allocations or measures implemented under MA63 as merely special considerations for Sabah and Sarawak.
Meanwhile, Abang Johari backed the proposal to place MA63 within a national framework, saying it would align provisions enshrined in the Federal Constitution with efforts to strengthen Malaysia’s unity.
“We want to align what is enshrined in the Constitution with the unity of Malaysia as a united nation, a united Malaysia, as we continue our efforts to develop the country,” he said.
He said the approach was more practical in balancing the interests of the Federal Government, Sabah and Sarawak, including in matters of finance and national development. — Bernama

Title: Sabah, Sarawak to get bigger share of Parliament seats, Anwar says as MA63 push moves ahead
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Sabah and Sarawak will get a higher proportion of parliamentary representation under a Cabinet decision in principle to increase the number of seats for the two Borneo states, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
Anwar said the Cabinet had agreed to increase the number of parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak, although the exact number and mechanism had yet to be determined.
He stressed that any increase must also raise the proportion of seats held by the two states to reflect the spirit of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63).
“An increase in the number of seats can be misleading. An increase does not necessarily mean that the ratio will improve; it could simply mean equalising the numbers.
“So the increase must be accompanied by an increase in the proportion of representation for Sabah and Sarawak,” he said in a press conference after chairing the committee meeting for the implementation of the MA63 with Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg present.
Anwar added that there could also be an increase in seats for peninsular Malaysia.
He said the Cabinet made the decision last Wednesday and the Election Commission had been informed to begin discussions on the mechanism and number of additional seats.
Representatives from the two states would subsequently negotiate with political parties from peninsular Malaysia on the details, Anwar said.
Under the original Malaysia Agreement 1963, when Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak and Malaya formed the Federation, the three territories collectively held one-third of the parliamentary seats to prevent Malaya from unilaterally securing the two-thirds majority required to amend the Federal Constitution.
That proportion was reduced after Singapore left the federation in 1965. Of the 222 parliamentary seats today, Sabah has 25 and Sarawak 31, giving the two states a combined 25 per cent of the total compared with 75 per cent for peninsular Malaysia.
Sabah and Sarawak have been seeking a minimum one-third, or 33 per cent, share of parliamentary representation, which would require about 18 additional seats.
“So now we need to look at the mechanism. The principle is that there must be an increase that raises the proportion of representation. We have agreed to that. But the details and mechanics will be discussed with the Election Commission and the various states and political parties,” Anwar said.
Asked whether the increased representation could be implemented before the next general election, Anwar said he was uncertain whether there would be sufficient time.
“I am not certain whether there will be sufficient time because we have to follow the process. I do not want to interfere with the constitutional process. But the important thing is that the decision has been made and the Election Commission has been informed,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar said the government was expediting the appointment of more Sabah- and Sarawak-born Malaysians to key government positions, another matter he said was recognised under MA63.
He said the first phase had already been implemented, while the second phase would be expedited.
Anwar described MA63 as a national commitment rather than an issue concerning only Sabah and Sarawak.
“I had proposed that discussions on MA63 be made part of the national narrative. This is very important because otherwise it becomes a sectoral matter that we have to discuss separately every year.
“It is a national commitment about development, stability, and the commitments we made at independence, Malaya in 1957 and Malaysia in 1963,” he said.
He said the issue should be viewed as part of efforts to strengthen Malaysia as a whole, rather than through the lens of race, political parties or regional interests.

Title: Zahid says Umno still hopes for favourable outcome after Najib clemency deferred
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today expressed disappointment over the postponement of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency application, but said the party continues to hope for a favourable outcome.
Zahid said Umno respected the decision and would continue to uphold the institution of the Malay Rulers while appealing to His Majesty the King to use his wisdom in deciding Najib’s application.
“We are saddened by the decision. Nevertheless, we continue to express our deepest respect to His Majesty the King, and we appeal to His Majesty to use all his wisdom to make the best decision.
“We continue to uphold the institution of the Malay Rulers. We continue to support the Rulers, and we hope that something favourable will be granted to Datuk Seri Najib Abdul Razak,” he told reporters after delivering his policy speech at Umno’s general assembly here.
The Prime Minister’s Department today said Najib’s clemency application had been deferred to a future sitting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board.
The department – which covers Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya – said the board held its 63rd meeting this morning with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim consenting to the postponement.
Earlier this morning Zahid expressed hope for the “best” news for Najib during his policy speech at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
Umno delegates greeted Najib’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, enthusiastically with applause after Zahid asked her to stand for a moment during his speech.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison and a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on August 23, 2022.
In 2024, the Federal Territories Pardons Board halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
Najib and his lawyers subsequently argued that the partial pardon included a royal addendum allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, and sued to have it enforced.
On December  22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest.
Najib withdrew his appeal against the decision in April this year.

Title: State institutions won’t be political tools if BN returns to power, Zahid pledges at Umno assembly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today vowed that Malaysia’s courts and institutions would not be used as political tools if Barisan Nasional (BN) returns to Putrajaya.
Zahid said the pledge was part of BN’s proposed “Agenda Malaysia Biru”, a roadmap of eight initiatives aimed at shaping the country as it approaches its centenary of independence.
“We want the people to trust the courts and not have the courts exploited. Investors should trust the regulations. Civil servants should trust the system and not be haunted by threats.
“And whoever forms the Government, state institutions must not be used as tools for political interests,” he said in his policy speech at Umno’s general assembly here.
Zahid said the initiative aimed to place Malaysia among the world’s top 20 countries in terms of integrity, governance and the rule of law.
“We want rule of law, not rule by law. Good governance is not merely a slogan in a manifesto.
“Instead, it is the belief that power is used as a trust and not as a means for oppression,” he said.
He said the agenda would be implemented if BN and Umno were given the mandate to lead Putrajaya again, with its eight initiatives focused on strengthening national wealth, human capital, ownership, well-being, crisis preparedness, public protection, institutional trust and national interests.
The agenda is built around four broad aspirations — a sovereign and united Malaysia; an innovative, high-income nation; a prosperous and equitable society; and a country that is respected and outstanding on the world stage.
Zahid said the initiatives were intended to guide Malaysia towards its centenary of independence while addressing the country’s economic, social and governance priorities.

Title: Anwar agrees Sarawak deserves fair share, promises formula clarity, interim measure by Malaysia Day
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim agreed to work towards establishing a formula for Sarawak to receive a share of the state’s revenue as he prepares to discuss an interim measure with Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg.
Anwar said Sarawak had put forward its views on a formula that would provide greater clarity on the matter, taking into account the federal government’s financial position and capacity.
“Sarawak has also put forward its views on a formula that should be introduced, so that the formula is clear and takes into account the country’s financial position and capacity, including what the minimum and maximum amounts that can be considered should be,” he said.
“I agree with this and have asked the federal and Sarawak finance ministry to discuss the introduction of such a formula,” he said to reporters after chairing a meeting of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) implementation committee here.
Anwar said he would continue discussions with Abang Johari over the next few days and hoped to announce an interim measure for Sarawak around the Malaysia Day celebrations in Kuching on September 16.
“Hopefully, after September 16, Malaysia Day in Kuching, I will be able to announce an interim measure for Sarawak,” he said.
The federal government has been in discussions with Sabah on how to fulfil its constitutional obligation to pay the latter 40 per cent of its state-derived revenue, which it has defaulted on since 1974.
In May, Anwar announced an RM1.5 billion interim special grant for Sabah as Putrajaya and the Sabah government continue negotiations over the implementation mechanism and the final sum.
Anwar said the same spirit of revenue return should be applied to Sarawak even though its financial arrangement does not have the same constitutional provision as Sabah.
Abang Johari welcomed the move, describing the proposed formula as a potential “win-win” arrangement between Sarawak and the federal government.
He said any arrangement should also take into account the financial stability of the country.
“If our country is doing well, naturally we will do well. If it is not doing well, we must also accept the reality so that the country’s financial stability can be maintained,” he said.

Title: Zara Qairina inquest: Handwriting expert defends journal analysis despite rival’s differing testimony
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — A document examiner stood by her findings on writings linked to Zara Qairina Mahathir, telling an inquest that the testimony of another forensic handwriting expert had not changed any of her conclusions.
Recalled witness Nurul Atiqah Mohd Noh said Dr Linthini Gannetion’s testimony had not altered any of her findings after she considered the expert’s evidence.
Nurul, the second deponent, was questioned by Deputy Public Prosecutor Dana Arabi Wazani during the inquest into the death of the 13-year-old student before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan on Thursday.
Dana:
Overall, after considering Dr Linthini’s testimony, is there anything in her testimony that caused you to change any of the conclusions contained in Exhibit I-31?
Nurul:
No.
Dana:
Dr Linthini also stated that in Y4B, part of the word “challenge” (“hallenge”) was written in pencil and the word “tauddin” in “Retauddin” may have been added later with a different pen, and that Y13A contained erased writing, including the phrase “Jala imut”. You concluded that Y4 and Y13 were written by the exemplar writer.
If there are scribbles, minor amendments or the use of different writing instruments on a small portion of an entry, in your opinion, does that alter the overall conclusion that the entry was written by Zara?
Nurul:
No.
Dana:
Dr Linthini emphasised that almost all the sheets from Y1 to Y15 were dated, except Y8B and Y13B, and described this as inconsistent with Zara’s habit of not always recording dates in her journal. In your opinion, is the frequency or pattern of writing dates a scientific criterion in forensic document examination for determining the writer or the existence of interference? Does the habit of writing dates not vary according to the type of entry, such as a daily journal entry compared with an entry addressed to someone, or according to the circumstances in which it was written?
Nurul:
The frequency or pattern of writing dates is a characteristic that can be observed, but it is not the only characteristic to prove the identity of a writer.
Nurul was also asked about differences between her findings and those of Dr Linthini Gannetion, a certified handwriting expert who was previously called by Zara’s mother to testify on the examination of the questioned writings.
Dana:
Dr Linthini stated that she used the “ACEV” method, namely Analysis, Comparison, Evaluation and Verification. Based on your understanding, what is done under this method, and is it essentially the same as the comparison method used by the Chemistry Department?
Nurul:
Based on my understanding, this method is the same.
Dana:
In your opinion, are the results of a handwriting examination determined solely by the use of instruments such as Video Spectral Comparator (VSC) or do they depend on the examiner’s skills in identifying, assessing and weighing the characteristics of handwriting?
Nurul:
The use of instruments such as VSC is to assist the examination. A comprehensive examination depends on the skills of the document examiner.
Dana:
Dr Linthini emphasised that the handwriting of a growing adolescent is volatile and can change within a short period, hence the most reliable comparison is with the most contemporary samples. Do you agree that a person’s handwriting can change over time?
Nurul:
Agree.
Dana:
If an adolescent’s handwriting is indeed volatile and changes over time, in your opinion, does every small difference in handwriting characteristics at a particular time necessarily indicate a different writer?
Nurul:
Not necessarily.
Dana:
Dr Linthini, in paragraph 25 of her witness statement, stated that she could not reach any conclusion regarding the writer of Y1A, Y1B, Y2A, Y2B, Y3A, Y3B, Y4A, Y4B, Y5A, Y5B, Y6A, Y6B, Y7A, Y7B, Y8A, Y9A, Y9B and Y10A, among others, due to the absence of contemporary handwriting samples for the period from November 2024 to January 2025.
In your opinion, does the opinion that “no conclusion can be made” mean that the writings were not written by the late Zara Qairina?
Nurul:
No.
Dana:
Does the opinion that “no conclusion can be made” mean that the writings were written by someone else?
Nurul:
No.
Dana:
In your previous testimony, you also stated that “Y1” to “Y7” and “Y9” to “Y15” were written by the same person. Is that correct?
Nurul:
Correct.
Dana: Please refer to paragraph 21(i) of your second report. Your conclusion was that the writings in W1, W2, W3 and Y1-Y15 were written by the exemplar writer, Zara Qairina Binti Mahathir, correct?
Nurul:
Correct.
Dana:
Dr Linthini stated that in W2, pages 45, 49 to 51, 58, 59, 61 and 62 contained writings by other individuals besides the late Zara, and she concluded that other people may have had access to W2.
After your comprehensive examination of W2, did you find any pages or portions of W2 that were not written by the exemplar writer?
Nurul:
There are writings with slightly different characteristics, but I cannot give an opinion on the writer because there are only a few characters.
Dana:
If most of the entries in a journal were written by its owner but there were several lines or entries written by another person, in your opinion, does that necessarily mean that the main entries in the journal were not written by its owner?
Nurul:
No.
Dana:
Dr Linthini agreed that pages 2, 7 to 14, 25 to 37, 46, 58 to 64, 73 to 84 and 86 to 89 of W3 were not written by the late Zara. So far, are Dr Linthini’s findings consistent with your findings?
Nurul:
Yes, consistent.
Dana:
In your opinion, does the absence of contemporary samples automatically prevent an examiner from reaching any conclusion, or does it depend on the quality, quantity and consistency of the characteristics of similarities found in the material examined?
Nurul:
It depends on the results of the examination, whether similarities or differences are found.
Dana:
Based solely on presumptive observations and without confirmatory tests such as ESDA or ink and paper analysis, in your opinion, can an examiner conclude that there are signs of interference in Y1 to Y15?
Nurul:
It depends on the type of interference found.
The inquest will resume in October. — Daily Express

Title: ‘Time has come for BN to lead’: Zahid demands GE16 held as soon as possible
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today called for the 16th General Election (GE16) to be held as soon as possible, saying the time had come for Barisan Nasional (BN) to seek a fresh mandate to lead the country.
Zahid said GE16 would be a defining moment for Umno and BN to regain the mandate to lead, as he outlined the coalition’s “gelombang biru” (blue wave) strategy ahead of the next general election.
“Therefore, the time has come for GE16 to be held immediately. Do you agree?” he said in his fiery policy speech at Umno’s general assembly here, to which delegates in the Dewan Merdeka hall replied with a loud “Yes!”.
He then told delegates that since the party had already been fighting for its political position, it should see the battle through to the end.
“Since we have started, we might as well see it through to the end. Since we are already fighting, let us fight all the way,” he said.
Zahid said the political landscape had become more complex, with Malay politics no longer centred on a single political vehicle and voter loyalties no longer being inherited.
He said the younger generation was also less bound by nostalgia for the old political landscape, meaning Umno could no longer rely on a single formula in every electoral battleground.
“Demographics differ. Issues differ. Candidates differ. Sentiments also differ. That is the reality today,” he said.
Zahid said the results in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan had each offered different lessons for the party.
He said Sabah had provided a lesson, Johor had raised confidence, while Negri Sembilan showed that political understanding could be a strength.
“Melaka, God willing, will be the next battleground to test how far the ‘blue wave’ can truly be translated into action,” he said.
Zahid said the blue wave was not merely intended to make Umno a supporting component of the government.
“GE16 is the defining moment for us to regain the mandate to lead the country,” he said.
GE16 must be held by 2028 at the latest, unless Parliament is dissolved earlier.

Title: Beyond data centres: What Budget 2027 needs to deliver, according to MBSB Investment Bank
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Budget 2027 should move Malaysia’s artificial intelligence (AI) agenda beyond data centre construction towards enterprise adoption, domestic intellectual property, cybersecurity and workforce productivity.
MBSB Investment Bank Bhd (MBSB IB) said there should also be focus on supply-side efficiency by broadening the tax base, closing leakages, expanding consumption excises, introducing carbon pricing, rationalising spending and crowding in private investment.
“Budget 2027 should not only be assessed through fiscal expenditure. It should also strengthen Malaysia’s broader investment ecosystem and the mobilisation of domestic capital,” it said in its Budget 2027 preview today.
MBSB IB emphasised that its wish list centres on policy certainty, transparent project implementation, outcome-based incentives and measures that channel long-term savings into productive investment.
“A successful budget would not merely provide near-term economic support, but it would improve access to growth capital, strengthen domestic capabilities and help translate Malaysia’s investment cycle into sustainable productivity, higher-quality employment and long-term economic value,” it added.
MBSB IB also emphasised that a multi-year project pipeline, with project values, tender timing, funding sources and execution milestones disclosed, should be published.
“This would improve planning and reduce speculative market movements,” it said.
Budget 2027 is scheduled to be tabled on Oct 9, 2026, and would be the fifth Madani Budget and the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan.
On the overall Budget 2027 allocation, MBSB IB said the budget is expected to remain moderately expansionary, with total federal government expenditure potentially reaching a new record of around RM440.9 billion, compared with Budget 2026’s RM421.2 billion.
“The larger allocation is likely to reflect higher operating expenditure, continued social and cost-of-living support, as well as higher development spending.
“Nevertheless, the increase is expected to remain measured as the government continues to balance the need to support economic growth with its medium-term fiscal consolidation objectives,” it said.
Development spending is expected to increase to between RM85 billion and RM90 billion, up from RM81 billion in Budget 2026.
On the fiscal deficit, MBSB IB said the deficit is expected to narrow to around 3.3 per cent to 3.5 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 2027.
Meanwhile, the investment bank said federal government revenue is expected to improve further in 2027, supported by increased direct and indirect tax collections on the back of sustained economic growth, continued efforts to broaden the revenue base and improved fiscal collections.
“For 2026, MOF had originally projected revenue of RM343.1 billion, underpinned by better tax collection and digitalisation initiatives. Total revenue is estimated to reach RM365.1 billion next year,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Health cooperation gets fresh push as Asean, China face new threats
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Asean and China are seeking to deepen their decade-long health cooperation as the region confronts emerging public health threats, climate change, demographic shifts and rapid technological transformation.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the partnership is entering an increasingly consequential chapter, with both sides working towards resilient, inclusive and sustainable health systems capable of responding to present and future challenges.
“Our gathering today comes at a defining moment as we face the rapidly evolving health landscape, shaped by emerging public health threats, climate change, demographic shifts and accelerating technological transformation.
“These challenges remind us that resilient health systems are no longer simply a national priority. They are a shared regional imperative,” he said.
He said this in his opening remarks when chairing the 10th Asean-China Health Ministers’ Meeting in conjunction with the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings here today.
The meeting was co-chaired with Vice-Minister of China’s National Health Commission Dr Liu Jinfeng.
Dzulkefly said discussions at the meeting, themed ‘Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future Ready Health Systems’, would also contribute to the implementation of the Asean Strategic Health Agenda (ASHA) 2026-2030 and translate common aspirations into practical action.
“The decisions and perspectives we share today have the potential to strengthen the health and resilience of more than two billion people across Asean and China.
“Let us seize this opportunity to build a decade of partnership and look ahead with renewed resolve to deepen our cooperation for the decades to come,” he added.
He said the meeting also aims to provide strategic direction in advancing the Asean-China Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) on health cooperation, capture collective commitments through a Joint Statement and ensure the partnership delivers tangible benefits to the people. — Bernama

Title: Zahid takes swipe at Pakatan petrol promise, blasts Budi95 policy flip‑flop, says Umno primed for GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today took a veiled jibe at Pakatan Harapan’s past election manifesto to slash petrol prices within 24 hours if the coalition won the general election.
Speaking at the 2026 Umno General Assembly today, Ahmad Zahid said Umno is a far-sighted party with a long-term vision for Malaysia rather than one that merely hopes to survive one election after another.
“We are starting again after a fall,” he said, referring to Umno’s disastrous outing in GE14, held in 2018.
“From once ruling the country and being a dominant force, we have experienced being the opposition and then sharing power.
“Now, we are ready to create another victory,” he added.
Stressing that Umno would not make unrealistic promises, Zahid said: “We are also not a party that says, menang hari ini (win today)…” as the crowd responded, “minyak turun (fuel prices down)”.
Similarly, he also took a swipe at the PH-led unity government’s flip-flopping approach in withdrawing and later reinstating the subsidised fuel quota to 300 litres under the Budi95 programme.
“First, they reduce the quota, then they reinstate it. Next, I think they will pull it back and restore it nearer to the next general election.
“Who is doing this? Guru,” he said, drawing thunderous applause from the audience.
Zahid did not elaborate on whom he meant by “guru”, though the remark was widely seen as a veiled reference to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“God willing, we will be able to perform better than Guru has done,” he added.

Title: No payslip, no problem? New housing policy targets gig workers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Providing homeownership assistance, particularly for youths and gig workers, is among the key priorities of the National Housing Policy (DRN) 2026-2035, ensuring greater access to affordable housing.
Ministry of Housing and Local Government (known by its Malay initials KPKT) Deputy Secretary-General (Housing and Urban Wellbeing) Zulkeflee Sulaiman said the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP) was among the mechanisms available to help first-time homebuyers without a fixed income or payslips.
“SJKP can help first-time homebuyers, particularly gig workers who do not have payslips, to secure housing loans, with the Government acting as a guarantor through participating banks.
“The Government wants to make sure young people who want to own their first home are not left behind,” he said when appearing as a guest on Bernama TV’s Ruang Bicara programme here yesterday.
Launched by Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming on Aug 10, the DRN 2026-2035 sets the direction for the national housing sector over the next decade, covering six focus areas, 17 strategies and 59 action plans.
Zulkeflee said the policy also includes measures to address strata management issues, with amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013 expected to be brought to the Government next year before being tabled in Parliament.
Meanwhile, KPKT Housing Planning Division undersecretary J. Murali said the ministry was refining the national affordable housing guidelines, with location being among the factors considered in determining prices.
He said setting RM300,000 as a nationwide benchmark might not be suitable, as affordability and market conditions varied between Kuala Lumpur and states such as Perlis, Sabah and Sarawak.
“We already have the framework and are now refining it. We will come up with national affordable housing guidelines which will be launched later,” he said.
Murali said that, apart from pricing, the ministry was also taking into account tenant welfare, despite the country’s 76 per cent homeownership rate.
As such, he said a Residential Tenancy Act would be introduced to provide clearer protection for tenants while also safeguarding property owners’ interests.
Murali said the DRN 2026-2035 would involve the drafting of three new pieces of legislation, namely the Property Development Act, Building Managers Act and Residential Tenancy Act, as well as amendments to the Strata Management Act 2013. — Bernama

Title: Pardons Board postpones decision on Najib’s clemency application
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 11 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency application has been deferred to a future sitting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board, the Prime Minister’s Department’s Legal Affairs Division (BHEUU) said today.
In a statement, it confirmed the board held its 63rd meeting this morning for Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya.
“The Yang di-Pertuan Agong also consented for Datuk Seri Mohd Najib bin Tun Haji Abdul Razak’s application for pardon to be postponed to a Pardons Board meeting that will be held in the future,” BHEUU said.
Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim consented to the release of 65 prisoners during the Pardons Board meeting, with all non-citizens ordered to be deported to their countries of origin within six months.

Title: Classic hits set upbeat tone as Umno assembly enters third day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — If the background music was anything to go by, spirits were soaring high on day three of the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL).
Guests and delegates who came as early as 7am were treated to a slew of local classic hits from the 1970s and 1980s as they made their way into the Dewan Merdeka of WTCKL following Umno’s flag raising ceremony and photo session.
From classic hits such as
Warisan
by Datuk Sudirman,
Ilham Pujangga
by Ismail Haron as well as
Seiring Sejalan
by the late Datuk Sharifah Aini featuring the late Broery Marantika.
The playlist was further elevated with the inclusion of upbeat tunes such as
Adikku Pandai Menari
by Aman Shah,
Selamat Pagi Sayang
by Noor Kumalasari as well as
Ratu Dansa
by Carefree.
The choice of songs may be coincidental; however, it nonetheless reflects Umno’s current position, particularly following its back to back win in the recent state elections in Negeri Sembilan and Johor.
The selection also reflects the renewed optimism within Umno’s ranks — elevated by Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Rahim joining the assembly after his release from remand.
Today will also mark the height of the four-day assembly as Umno’s Supreme Council members are set for a motion debate following the presidential policy speech by party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Aside from that, the assembly today also hosted four PAS leaders including its vice president Datuk Idris Ahmad, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, PAS information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari and its assistant secretary-general Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman.

Title: A promise that cannot be kept: Grief and gratitude pour in for Sarawak's fallen medics
Article:
MIRI, Sept 11 — “This story may soon be forgotten by others, bit by bit, but I will never forget you, not even for a second.”
Those were the anguished words posted on Threads by izzatisyamimi, wife of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30, who was among five people killed when a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crashed near Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, on Sept 8.
Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
Posting under the handle izzatisyamimi shortly after midnight on Sept 10, just hours after her husband’s DNA sample was sent for testing and a day after his body was recovered, the widow poured out her grief in a message that has since been widely shared on social media.
“People see me as strong on the outside, but inside I am completely shattered,” she wrote. “You always said I was a supermom, you always said I was a strong woman, but who am I without you by my side? You taught me to be strong, but it isn’t fair of you to leave me like this. I did tell you to fly high, but this time you flew too high — so high that I can no longer catch up with you. Love you always.”
A day earlier, as the bodies of the victims were being recovered from the crash site, the same account had posted another message addressed directly to her late husband, describing the couple’s children crying inconsolably through the night.
“Your children really aren’t giving me any chance to cry at all, are they? Please help settle them for a while, daddy — my pool of tears is already full. It’s my turn now. Tonight both of them were wailing. Just be patient, it’s my turn now. I hope you’re strong enough to watch me cry my heart out. We love you daddy,” she wrote.
The others who died in their FDS mission to serve the rural people of Sarawak were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
The tragedy has also prompted an outpouring of recollections from villagers, former colleagues, friends and family members of the crew, many of whom took to social media to share memories of the FDS team’s outreach trips across Kapit, Limbang and Miri divisions.
Among the widely circulated tributes was a video and photo montage sourced from TikTok user Fikri Jalil, showing the FDS team during a visit to Kampung Balai in Ulu Baram.
Among the images were a doctor attending to a patient on the steps of a longhouse, villagers chatting warmly with the pilot during a stopover, and locals helping the crew load medical supplies and equipment back onto the aircraft.
The accompanying caption recalled the crew’s parting words to the villagers: “We’ll come again in November, okay?”
“These, it turned out, were the last words spoken before they left Kampung Balai, Ulu Baram,” the post read. “That promise, now impossible to keep, has become a heart-wrenching memory for villagers still grieving over this tragedy. Their service and sacrifice to the villagers will never be forgotten. Al-Fatihah.”
Among the five victims was paramedic the late Jessie Paya Jok, 44, who according to a close friend had been just months away from beginning a new chapter in her life.
Her friend of nearly two decades, Caroline Sawai Joseph Chungat, said Paya had excitedly shared that this month was to be her last serving with the FDS. She had planned to pursue an Advanced Diploma in Midwifery thereafter.
“Next year I want to continue my studies…” was how Paya had put it to those close to her, Chungat recalled — an ambition that never came to pass.
Chungat, who had known Paya since 2005, described her as a soft-spoken woman of few words who nonetheless brightened the lives of those around her with her smile. During her service at the Bario Health Clinic, Paya was remembered fondly by residents of the interior, including for reportedly using her own money at times to help cover the travel fares of patients who needed treatment at Miri Hospital.
“Not everyone’s good deeds are spoken of while they are still alive. Sometimes, it is only after they are gone that we truly realise the extent of the kindness they showed,” Chungat’s tribute read, adding that although Paya’s dream went unfulfilled, her service and kindness would continue to be remembered by those whose lives she touched.
“Al-Fatihah for the late Jessie Paya Jok. May all her sacrifices become deeds that continue to bring reward,” the tribute concluded.
The helicopter, which was ferrying an FDS medical team, went down near Long Lellang in Ulu Baram on Sept 8, killing all five people on board. Recovery operations for the victims’ remains were carried out over the following days, with DNA samples taken to confirm their identities.
The FDS provides outreach medical and health services to remote interior communities across Sarawak, with teams regularly flown by helicopter to longhouses and villages inaccessible by road. — The Borneo Post

Title: Haze can’t stop the party: Sabah moves Malaysia Day celebration to SICC
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 11 — The Sabah-level Malaysia Day celebration on Sept 16 would be moved to the Sabah International Convention Centre (SICC) due to haze.
State Tourism, Culture and Environment Minister Datuk Jafry Ariffin said the change of venue was made to ensure the celebration could proceed as planned.
“We have decided to move the celebration to SICC due to the haze affecting the State and the country.
“The matter has been agreed upon by the State Cabinet.
As one of Sabah's key business and trade platforms, SIE2026 has attracted participation from 15 countries and features 300 exhibition booths, with approximately 35 per cent involving international exhibitors.
“The celebration will begin at 8pm and will take place simultaneously with the national-level celebration in Kuching, Sarawak. Various exciting activities have been planned to enliven the celebration.
“Among them are dance performances, a Malaysia Madani presentation montage and entertainment by local artistes,” Jafry said after paying a courtesy call on Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Musa Aman at Istana Seri Kinabalu.
The courtesy call was to seek Tun Musa’s consent to attend the Sabah-level Malaysia Day celebration.
Meanwhile, Jafry said Malaysia Day celebrations are being held by several agencies, particularly the State Archives.
“The celebration organised by the State Archives is ongoing and will end this Friday.
“The State Archives is holding an exhibition on the history of Malaysia Day,” he said.
He invited the public, particularly Kota Kinabalu residents and those in nearby areas, to attend and enliven the Malaysia Day celebration on Sept 16. — Daily Express

Title: Haze bites: 14 areas nationwide hit unhealthy air levels, 11 of them in Sarawak alone
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — A total of 14 areas nationwide, including 11 in Sarawak, recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings due to haze as of 9 am today.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System portal, the areas in Sarawak with unhealthy readings are IPD Serian (197), Kuching (181), Samarahan (179), Sri Aman (172), Sarikei (163), Samalaju (161), Sibu (157), Mukah (155), Bintulu (153), Miri (147) and ILP Miri (147).
The other areas recording unhealthy API levels are Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic in Sabah with a reading of 150, followed by Pasir Gudang in Johor (109) and the Federal Territory of Labuan (103).
Forty-nine areas nationwide were reported to have moderate air quality, while five areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 indicates moderate air quality, 101 to 200 indicates unhealthy air quality, 201 to 300 indicates very unhealthy air quality, while readings of 301 and above are considered hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Rosmah Mansor draws applause at Umno assembly as Najib’s clemency bid looms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, the wife of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, attended Umno’s general assembly today amid his bid for clemency.
Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi then invited Rosmah to stand as delegates in Dewan Merdeka applauded and showed their appreciation.
“Hopefully there will be the best news today, God willing,” Zahid said when opening his policy speech, drawing thunderous applause from the hall.
Rosmah was seated next to Zahid’s wife, Datin Seri Hamidah Khamis.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to convene this morning.
FMT previously reported that former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application is expected to be among the primary matters tabled before the board during this week’s sitting.
It remains unclear whether the board will arrive at an immediate decision or limit the session to preliminary deliberations.
A separate source indicated that the possibility of allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison term under house arrest may be broached, though it is uncertain whether that option will be formally deliberated during the morning meeting.
Yesterday, Zahid said he was hoping for the “best” outcome today for Najib’s latest application.
Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine. He began serving his sentence at Kajang Prison on Aug 23, 2022.
In 2024, the FT Pardons Board halved his prison term to six years and reduced the fine to RM50 million.
However, Najib and his lawyers subsequently insisted that the partial pardon came with a royal addendum for him to serve out his remaining time at home, eventually suing to have this granted.
On Dec 22 last year, High Court judge Alice Loke dismissed Najib’s application to serve the remainder of his reduced sentence under house arrest. Najib withdrew his appeal against the decision in April this year.
